references.text: The priests and Levites were to judge difficult cases and teach the people the Lord's law and statutes.
The people were commanded to follow what the priests and Levites taught them, as Moses had ordered.
The tribe of Levi was given the task of teaching Jacob the Lord's statutes and Israel his law.
The Levites were sent out to teach from the Book of the Law in all the cities of Judah.
Ezra the priest read the law to the people and explained it, so that they understood the Scripture.
The priests were to teach the people the difference between holy and common, between clean and unclean.
The lips of a priest should preserve knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth, for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.
Paul urges Timothy to entrust what he has heard to faithful people who will be able to teach others.
Believers should eventually become teachers themselves and be able to instruct others in God's word.
